A 70 year old diner, a brand new counter

The room everyone remembers

The Sunset Restaurant ran on St. Paul Street for about 70 years. Sunset Steak & Cheese took over the space and kept what made it the Sunset: the original booths and the vintage sign.

A fine dining chef, a flat top grill

The counter is run by chef Zach Smith of Michelin recommended Fat Rabbit. The cooking is diner cooking done properly: steak chopped on the grill, cheese melted through, rolls filled to the edge.

Opened 20 November 2026

Sunset Steak & Cheese opened on Friday 20 November 2026. Takeout through the afternoon, dine in until midnight, in the booths that were always there.

Watch the grill build the sandwich

Every cheesesteak here is built on the flat top, in order. Keep scrolling and watch one come together, layer by layer.

Steak downShaved steak hits the flat top and gets chopped as it sears.
Onions, peppersOnions and peppers fold through the steak on the grill.
Cheese pullCooper Sharp or Cheez Whiz, melted right through the pile.
Into the rollThe whole pile lands in the roll. That is a Sunset cheesesteak.

Illustrated build. The grill photo behind it is illustrative too.

The menu

Sandwiches first, the way the counter runs. Built on the grill, filled to the edge.

The Big Coop Cooper Sharp

Grilled steak piled into a roll with Cooper Sharp melted through it. Sharp and rich.

The Wizzard Cheez Whiz

The Philly classic, done the old way. Steak and onions under a ladle of Cheez Whiz.

Classic Philly Cheesesteak

Shaved steak chopped on the flat top with onions and peppers, cheese melted through, in a fresh roll.

Roast Pork and Rapini

Slow roast pork with rapini greens, the other great Philadelphia sandwich, served hot.

Italian Subs

Italian style subs built to order at the counter, stacked and dressed.

Chicago Dogs

Hot dogs dressed Chicago style, loaded with the full works of toppings.

Plus cold beer and cocktails

Dine in runs to midnight, and the counter pours cold beer and cocktails alongside the sandwiches, shakes and fries.
